title: In Fenway finale, Yankees’ Jazz Chisholm Jr. gets ejected on check-swing call
content:
BOSTON — It has been a frustrating and embarrassing weekend for the New York Yankees.

On Friday, Boston Red Sox starter Payton Tolle carried a no-hitter into the sixth inning. On Saturday, Red Sox starter Jake Bennett had a no-hitter into the fifth inning. And in Sunday’s 5-4 extra-innings loss, Red Sox starter Sonny Gray continued the trend with his own dominant performance.

Emotions on New York’s side boiled over in the finale, when Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. was ejected in the top of the sixth after arguing a strikeout on a checked swing. Chisholm was upset that home plate umpire Adam Hamari rang him up, rather than appeal to third base umpire Clint Vondrak for help.

Both Yankees manager Aaron Boone and first base coach Dan Fiorito sprinted to Chisholm to get between him and Hamari, but there was nothing they could do to prevent the second baseman from slamming his helmet into the dirt. Hamari actually missed Chisholm’s helmet toss while arguing with Boone, so it was first base umpire Todd Tichenor who ejected the player.

“Trying to keep him in the game in that situation, obviously trying to distract a little bit,” Boone said. “They gave him a little bit of rope out there, arguing his case. The helmet going in a certain direction probably cost him.”

Chisholm was unavailable to reporters after the game. His locker was cleaned out by the time media entered the visitor’s clubhouse. A Yankees public relations staffer said the second baseman chose to leave without addressing his ejection.

While it was reasonable for Chisholm to express displeasure with the call, it was not a smart decision. The Yankees’ offense is already down Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton and Trent Grisham, meaning offense has been hard to come by. Losing their leadoff hitter in a must-win game to avoid a sweep only compounded that.

“I never like our guys getting tossed,” Boone said. “Every once in a while, a guy does get tossed, though. Certainly don’t want him out of the game, obviously. Once the helmet bounces a certain way and they’ve given you a little bit of leeway, you’ve got to try and reign it in there.”

Anthony Volpe replaced Chisholm in the lineup, while José Caballero slid over from shortstop to second base.
